mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating rocky pebbles and then collapsing the swarm showed a satisfying way around the sticking barrier.

leastWorthwhile.text: The icy route repeated the rocky route, with mostly forced choices, although its mixed rock-and-ice composition added a useful distinction.

surprise.text: Gas drag can change pebble orbits and help concentrate solids rather than simply slowing their growth.

arbitrary.text: The icy path skipped a separate drag step even though its result described gas drag; the purpose was clear, but the difference from the rocky sequence felt a little arbitrary.

continue.text: Yes. The explanation of how gravity overcomes the sticking barrier makes me curious how these small bodies develop into worlds, despite the repetitive icy sequence.
